description: Analog partition testbenches: every committed SPICE deck behind a recorded analog measurement, every committed `klt sim` request that drives one, and the solve procedure's own Python bench (`sim/solve/`), which post-processes those surfaces into the rows 1-4 estimate and the item-6 yield figures without re-simulating. Cold starts are bounded by construction and do NOT re-run the multi-hour batch-fleet grids: the oscillator-bank and smoke decks run their real single-corner `ngspice -b` locally (--no-record, so a repeat appends nothing to the append-only records), the `sim/solve/` unittest suites run for real (they are pure post-processing on committed inputs), and every `klt sim` request is validated with `--dry-run` (deck staging, model resolution, corner/Monte-Carlo expansion against the pinned PDK) rather than simulated. The full fleet invocation for each grid is documented in that bench's README or `RECORD-*.md` and in manifests/README.md; it is not executed by this attestation. Being inventoried means the file is pinned by content hash and its declared cold start exited 0 -- not that a fleet run of it was recorded: 20 of the 140 `sim/solve/mc/requests-sized/` requests (the tt/1.62V/-40C chunks) are committed, drift-checked and never run, as sim/solve/mc/RECORD-2026-11-06-item6-sized-partial.md states. What each cold start does and does not cover is tabulated in manifests/README.md, "Item 9 (testbenches shipped)".
